full_story_part1.canonical_text:
The quiet problem starts after the shopping is done.

Fruit and vegetables go into the refrigerator. They may look safe inside the crisper drawer. But that drawer may have a small slider or dial. It is not just decoration.

Many refrigerators offer two settings: high humidity and low humidity. Each setting has a different job.

High humidity keeps the drawer more closed. This helps hold water around the food. It is useful for vegetables, especially leafy greens. These vegetables lose water quickly. When that happens, they become dry and wilt.

full_story_part2.text: Low humidity allows more air to move through the drawer. This is important for fruit. As fruit becomes ripe, it gives off a natural gas called ethylene. If this gas stays around other fruit and vegetables, they may become ripe too quickly. Then they can go bad sooner. A low-humidity drawer lets the gas escape more easily. This can help the food around the fruit last longer. So the basic rule is simple: Fruit usually goes in low humidity. Vegetables, especially leafy greens, usually go in high humidity. It is a small change. But it gives each type of food the environment it needs.
